title: CareerOrbit

title: TechFarming
summary: A B.Tech agricultural-rover research project, co-authored in IJESAT in 2023, followed by a connected-agriculture web-platform extension.
problem: Soil-moisture checks and plant-health inspection can require repeated manual fieldwork. The academic project explored remote sensing and camera-based cotton-leaf disease classification.
approach: The 2023 paper describes a remotely controlled rover with a robotic arm, soil-moisture sensor and live camera. Its MATLAB image-analysis pipeline uses K-means segmentation, GLCM features and SVM classification. Later web-platform work added accounts, device registration and sensor-report history.
contribution: Co-author of the 2023 research paper and contributor to the B.Tech hardware/software project. Subsequently contributed to supporting web-platform enhancements, integration testing, troubleshooting and documentation. The publication describes the team’s work; it does not assign individual ownership of each subsystem.

publication.title: Design and Development of Rover with Robotic Arm-based Soil Moisture Sensor and Live Camera for Plant Health Monitoring
publication.authors: K. Prem Sagar, Siripaka Rakesh, P. Sathish Reddy, Lungchuingam and G. Abhinav Kumar
publication.note: The paper documents a team research prototype and MATLAB demonstrations. It does not establish that the current web application runs the classifier, controls the rover or receives live readings from the original hardware.

phases.title: 2023 · Academic rover research
phases.description: Robotic-arm soil-moisture sensing, live-camera plant monitoring and a MATLAB cotton-leaf classification pipeline, documented in the co-authored paper.

phases.title: Later · Web-platform extension
phases.description: React/Express/MySQL account and device workflows, validated reporting APIs and reading history. Physical hardware integration and classifier deployment require separate verification.

imageAlt: Rover assembly CAD model reproduced from the 2023 TechFarming research paper, page 243

research.intro: An agricultural rover combining remote movement, robotic-arm soil-moisture sensing and camera-based cotton-leaf analysis. The details and original figures below come from the 2023 team publication.

hardware.name: Arduino Uno
hardware.detail: Controller named in the proposed system block diagram.

hardware.name: Robotic arm + soil-moisture sensor
hardware.detail: Positions the probe and inserts it into the soil for a moisture measurement. The paper discusses capacitive or resistive sensing without naming a specific sensor model.

hardware.name: Live camera
hardware.detail: Captures plant images for monitoring and subsequent analysis; the camera model and interface are not specified.

hardware.name: Left/right motors + motor driver
hardware.detail: Provide remotely controlled rover movement. The block diagram shows a 12 V DC supply for the motor stage.

hardware.name: Six-channel transmitter + receiver
hardware.detail: Remote-control link described for operating the rover. No transmitter or receiver part number is given.

hardware.name: Power supplies
hardware.detail: The diagram labels 12 V DC and 5 V DC supplies. A CAD image depicts a battery marked 12 V 7.2 Ah; this is a design illustration, not a measured runtime result.

steps.title: Acquire cotton-leaf images
steps.detail: Camera images are stored in JPG format for the image-analysis stage.

steps.title: Preprocess the images
steps.detail: The paper describes median filtering and conversion from RGB to grayscale.

steps.title: Segment with K-means
steps.detail: Group pixels into clusters to isolate regions showing disease symptoms.

steps.title: Extract image features
steps.detail: Use GLCM-based texture analysis and statistical features. The paper lists 13 discriminating features.

steps.title: Classify with SVM
steps.detail: Apply multiclass support vector machine classification to the extracted cotton-leaf features.

steps.title: Inspect MATLAB output
steps.detail: The reported demonstrations use MATLAB R2014a. The figures show cluster selection and the MATLAB execution environment.

research.limits: The publication does not provide firmware pin assignments, exact sensor/camera part numbers, a verified field-accuracy benchmark or evidence that the later website controls the rover. These require original hardware records and separate validation.
